niche.habitat: Fractured salt pavements, Lane edges where evaporite crust is thin. Also, in the council's sketch (no such creature in this world yet): Karrow, krelm uses a muscular cam to drive a rotating cap; Karrow evolved a vascularized free axle later. Krelm is the living fossil of the intermediate step.
niche.diet: Sub-crustal lichens, mineral salts, trapped detritus
niche.active: Diurnal, thermally active mid-day when crust is brittle

body: Asymmetrical ovoid, heavy rotating ventral molar cap, two short steering limbs, sensory stalks, keratinous cam-drive

links: Evaporite pans form endless flat crust

skill.effect: It spins its grinding molar cap, tearing into nearby enemies and strongly shattering their protective plating.

chains.weakness: Cap Jam: Gravel or soft mud fills the cam gap, locking the cap for 4s and leaving the creature helpless.
observe: Cap rotates independently of body rotation
Cap scrapes visible crust flakes and dust
Muscle pulses drive cam, not free spin

journal.en: It grinds its belly to reach the world's meat.

plausibility.summary: Make the cap a dead, periodically shed keratin-mineral rasp (silica or magnetite grit at the working face), grown from and driven by a stationary vascular collar rather than living tissue across the joint; specify that Lane-edge crust is thin and translucent enough for the photobiont. Strip damage/percentage stats from Grind per the frame's no-game-numbers rule; keep a plain 'rotary scrape' description.

moments: A Krelm grinds down a skirl, but gets its cap jammed by the skirl's keratin sheath and freezes as a slow target.

journal.en: Krelm can be befriended by offering salt crystals to grease the cam.
